summary: Iteration 008 adds bidirectional speech to Bay-Max: a full speech input pipeline (Microphone -> Silero VAD -> faster-whisper ASR -> echo suppression -> dialogue) integrated into the live runtime alongside existing TTS output. The audio package provides modular abstractions for microphone capture, voice activity detection, ASR transcription, and echo suppression, with Null* stubs for headless/CI testing. Spoken user turns enter the same session/memory path as typed turns (source='speech'). A speaking lock discards mic audio while TTS is active, with a configurable post-speech cooldown. A Baymax-inspired companion persona style guide is injected into the system prompt for calm, gentle, literal tone. Two new API endpoints (GET /v1/audio/status, GET /v1/stt/backends) expose speech-input state. Push-to-talk mode is supported alongside continuous VAD. All 356 automated tests pass (296 existing + 60 new). Lint clean. Manual hardware tests (VT801-VT810) are honestly marked not_run — Sol is a headless HPC machine with no microphone or speakers.

speech_input_backends.notes: Default real ASR backend. Lazy-loads WhisperModel on first transcription. Transcription of silence verified in automated tests. Real speech transcription requires microphone hardware (not available on Sol).
Always available. Used for headless/CI testing. Returns TranscriptionResult with success=False.

vad_backends.notes: Default VAD backend. State machine with IDLE/SPEECH_STARTED/SPEECH_ONGOING/SILENCE_AFTER_SPEECH states. Configurable threshold (0.65), min speech duration (300ms), silence timeout (500ms).
Always returns is_speech=True. Used for testing and push-to-talk mode bypass.

Silero VAD threshold (0.65) may need tuning for different microphone hardware and ambient noise levels
faster-whisper base.en model may struggle with accented English or multilingual input
